transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um... well, I suppose I'm here because of a bit of an ongoing situation at my apartment. I really don't want to come across as a difficult person—I've always prided myself on being very cooperative and level-headed. 

But... well, for months now, the property manager and certain people in the building have been doing things to pressure me out of the apartment. I hope it's okay to bring this up right away? It's just that it's been happening so much. It's this constant stream of misdelivered mail, and these very specifically timed noises in the walls, and little comments from neighbors that are... well, they're not accidents. 

They keep offering me paperwork and various explanations to try and brush it all off, but my background is in management analysis, so I'm very used to looking at data. And no amount of their paperwork or explanations changes the clear pattern I can see. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things properly and giving you the right kind of information.
Can you tell me more about why you believe these things are being done to you? Do you feel like these actions are intentionally targeted at you to harm or pressure you?

Oh, well... I wouldn't use a strong word like "harm." I really don't want to sound dramatic or—or accuse anyone of being truly malicious. I'm sure they aren't bad people, Doctor. I try to always see the best in others, and I certainly don't want to be a nuisance to management. 

As for why they're doing it... I honestly couldn't tell you. I've tried to figure that out myself, looking at all the variables, but... I just don't know. I've always paid my rent on time, I keep my apartment very clean, and I'm very quiet. Maybe they just want to renovate my unit and charge a higher rate to someone else? I really hesitate to even guess, because I don't want to make unfair assumptions or come across as... well, paranoid. 

I just know what the data shows—the clear pattern of the noises and the mail—even if I don't fully understand the motive behind it. I hope I don't sound unreasonable saying all this? I just want to be as helpful and accurate as possible for you, and I hope I'm answering your questions the right way.
Have you ever felt like things in your environment were happening specifically to send you a message or communicate something directly to you, even if others might not see it that way?

Oh, um... a message? No, I wouldn't say that at all. I really hope I haven't given you the impression that I think the universe is speaking to me or anything like that. I know how that sounds, and I certainly don't believe anything... unusual or supernatural is happening. 

I'm just a very observant person, you know? With my background, I'm trained to notice small discrepancies, like the mail and the noises. But I don't think it's a secret code or a message meant just for me. It's just... well, it's just the property management doing what they're doing to get me to leave. 

I really try to keep things grounded in facts and data, Doctor. I wouldn't want you to think I'm jumping to strange conclusions. Does that make sense? I hope I'm being clear about the difference.
You mentioned noises in the walls—can you describe them in more detail? Are they happening right now, or do you usually notice them at specific times?

Oh, um... well, no, they certainly aren't happening right now. It's very peaceful here in your office, actually, which I really appreciate. 

As for describing them... I'm actually not entirely sure how to give you a perfect description. I really wish I had more specific data for you. They're just... well, muffled thuds or scraping sounds. Just normal apartment sounds, really. I wouldn't want to exaggerate them or make them sound like something out of a movie, I promise! I try very hard not to be overly sensitive to every little creak in the building. 

And for the times... I haven't really kept a strict schedule of when they occur, mostly because I don't want to be one of those obsessive tenants who complains about everything. I suppose they just happen when they happen, usually when I'm trying to concentrate or read. 

I hope that's not too vague of an answer? I know you're trying to get a clear picture, and I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. Is that the sort of detail you were looking for, Doctor?
Have you ever experienced episodes where these kinds of concerns or experiences interfered with your ability to work, take care of daily tasks, or interact with others?

Oh, well... "interfered" is such a strong word. I really want to be careful not to sound like I'm falling apart or anything like that. I'm usually very organized and capable, Doctor, I promise. I don't want you to think I can't handle my life.

But, um... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest, and I do want to give you the most accurate picture I can... it has shifted my schedule a bit. Just a little. I've, well, I've pulled back from a few of my consulting jobs recently. Not because I can't do the work! I just... I felt I needed to prioritize figuring this out. 

So, I do spend a fair amount of my week now, um, following up with neighbors, or calling the building staff and the management office. Just trying to have polite conversations, of course! Nothing confrontational. But it does take time away from my normal work, and I haven't been keeping up with my painting routine like I usually do. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound obsessive or—or like I'm not functioning properly. I'm just trying to be thorough and resolve the situation so I can get back to normal. Is it okay that I've stepped back from work a little to handle this? I hope I'm making the right choices here.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt unusually energetic, overly confident, or irritable, where you were doing more things than usual or felt like you didn't need much sleep?

Oh, my goodness, no. No, I wouldn't say I've ever felt like that. "Overly confident" or not needing sleep—that sounds quite extreme, doesn't it? I really hope I haven't given you the impression that I'm prone to... well, to acting out of control or being manic. I know how important it is to maintain a balanced temperament, especially at my age and in my line of work. 

I've always been a very steady person, Doctor. I make sure to get my seven or eight hours of sleep every night, and I certainly don't go around feeling unusually energetic or doing a million things at once. I like to take my time and do things properly. 

I might get a little frustrated sometimes when the management office doesn't return my calls, but just normal frustration, you know? Nothing out of the ordinary. I really try to be pleasant with everyone. 

I hope that answers your question? I just want to reassure you that I'm very stable in my moods. I wouldn't want you to think I'm prone to wild swings or anything like that. Is that the kind of stability you're looking for?
Have there been times when others have told you that your concerns about the property management and neighbors were not accurate or unfounded, and yet you still believed them to be true?

Oh... um. Well, yes, I suppose some people have said things like that. My sister, for instance, thinks I'm making too much of it, and the building staff always have some sort of paperwork or... or a perfectly polite explanation for everything. 

I really hate to disagree with people, Doctor. I really do. I don't want to be difficult or stubborn. I know it must sound awful that I don't just take their word for it. I hope you don't think I'm just being paranoid or unreasonable. 

But... well, it's just that I can see the pattern, you know? It's been going on for months now. The misdelivered mail, the noises in the walls that happen right when I sit down, the little comments the neighbors make in the hallway... it's all just so coordinated. It really feels like the property manager and certain people in the building are trying to pressure me out of my apartment. 

I know they deny it, and I know I should probably just believe them, but... no amount of their explanations really changes what I'm experiencing. I'm sorry, I know that sounds terrible, like I'm ignoring the facts. I really am trying to look at this objectively, as an analyst would. 

Does that make sense, Doctor? I'm not trying to be difficult, I just... I can't unsee the pattern they've created. Am I explaining this clearly enough for you?
Have you ever had beliefs or concerns that others have told you are not true, outside of this situation with the property management and your neighbors?

Oh, um... no. No, nothing else like that. I really want to be clear about that, Doctor. I've never had any other... well, any other disagreements with people about what's real or what's happening. 

I've always been very grounded. In my work as an analyst, you have to rely on facts and data, and I've always prided myself on being very rational. I've never had anyone tell me I was imagining things or... or holding onto strange beliefs before this whole situation with the apartment started. 

I really hope this shows you that I'm not the kind of person who just makes things up or gets carried away with wild ideas. This current issue is very specific, and it's based on what I'm actually observing here in the building. 

I've always had a very good grasp on reality, I promise. I wouldn't want you to think this is some sort of lifelong habit of mine, being at odds with everyone else. Is that helpful to know? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right context so you can see I'm usually a very reasonable person.
Have you ever believed something very strongly that most people would find strange or impossible, like thoughts being placed in your mind, or being controlled by outside forces?

Oh, goodness, no. No, absolutely nothing like that. Thoughts being placed in my mind or being controlled by outside forces... that sounds like something out of a science fiction movie, doesn't it? I would never think anything like that.

I hope I haven't given you any reason to suspect I'd have those kinds of thoughts. I know how important it is to keep a clear head, and I assure you, my mind is entirely my own. As an analyst, my mind is my most important tool, and I take great care to be completely rational and independent in my thinking. 

I've never experienced anything bizarre or impossible like that. The situation with the property manager, well, that's just people behaving badly in the real world, you know? It's tangible. It's not some invisible force or anything strange. 

I really hope you can see the distinction I'm making. I'm a very practical, down-to-earth person. I wouldn't want you to think I'm losing my grip on reality or having truly bizarre ideas. I'm just dealing with a very difficult housing situation. Does that help clarify things? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right impression.
Have you ever had a belief that you knew wasn’t true or that others strongly disagreed with, even if you couldn’t explain exactly why you felt that way?

Oh, um... no. No, I haven't. I mean, if I couldn't explain why I felt a certain way, I don't think I would hold onto it, you know? 

I really try to make sure I have solid reasons for everything I think or do. Like I mentioned, with my background, I'm just so used to relying on the facts. If someone disagreed with me and I couldn't point to exactly why I believed something, I'd probably just assume I was wrong and let it go. I certainly wouldn't want to argue with anyone over something I couldn't even explain. 

I hope that makes sense. I just... I really want you to know that I'm not the type to just stubbornly cling to things for no reason. I always try to be logical. Is that the kind of answer you were looking for, Doctor? I want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Have you ever had a belief that others strongly disagreed with, even if you were aware that it might not be fully supported by facts or reality, outside of this situation with your apartment?

No, no, I... I really haven't. I mean, outside of what's happening here in the building, I've never held onto anything that wasn't completely backed up by facts. 

I know sometimes people can get, well, a little stubborn about their opinions, but I've always tried to be the kind of person who listens to reason. If I didn't have proof for something, and everyone else was telling me I was wrong... well, I'd feel quite foolish, wouldn't I? I wouldn't want anyone to think I was being difficult or irrational. 

I've spent my whole career making sure my assessments were completely grounded in reality. I really pride myself on that. So, no, I've never clung to a belief knowing it might not be true. I hope that reassures you, Doctor. I'm really trying to be as transparent as possible—am I giving you the information you need?
